summary: Sharp TTFB spike for chat completions observed after hybrid runtime/quantized-model handoff
description:
Issue summary: After a hybrid runtime rollout that enabled automated handoff to a quantized variant for cost-savings, Ledgerly reported a pronounced increase in TTFB for chat completions. The surge began at ~09:15 PDT and impacted ~30% of their chat requests, with some requests timing out at the CDN layer. This appears correlated with model handoffs during autoscaling events and peak concurrent sessions.

Impact: Customer-facing chat UI experiences 5-10s additional delay for first token; several sessions hit streaming timeouts and customers reported degraded UX during business hours. Customer is on Dedicated capacity and relies on pinned fleet with autoscale burst enabled.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Using Ledgerly prod account on dedicated pool in us-east-1, create chat session with long system prompt (~2k tokens).
2) Send first user message concurrently from 6 clients to trigger autoscale and handoff (simulated concurrency).
3) Observe time-to-first-token metric in Console/Per-route view and the streaming connection for slow start or 504s.
4) Repeat during scheduled autoscale window (09:00-10:00 PDT) to reproduce increased incidence.
impact: ~30% of chat completion requests for Ledgerly see 3-10s extra TTFB; overall customer SLA breach risk for P1 if unresolved; increased support load and potential revenue impact for high-traffic flow.
logs: Gateway 5xx/504 spike between 09:14:08 and 09:27:12 PDT. Sample request ids: req_56a2, req_56a7, req_56c3.
Serving logs show repeated model-variant transition events: handoff_start=model_swap_2026-03-01T09:13:59Z, handoff_complete delayed by 1.2-2.4s on affected workers.
KV-cache miss ratio increased from 12% to 67% during window for rw-13b-quant-pt-v2.
Kernel selection fallback entries: attempted optimized-quant-kernel -> fallback to generic-kernel due to shape mismatch on first batch.
timeline: 2026-03-01 09:12 PDT - Ledgerly reports first user complaints to CS via support form.
2026-03-01 09:15 PDT - Alert: per-route TTFB > 2s threshold for ledgerly/chat-route in us-east-1 (Grafana alert GRAF-8734).
2026-03-01 09:22 PDT - SRE/Support triage call. Identified correlation with recent hybrid runtime push enabling quantized variant handoffs (release tag: runtime-2.18.0).
2026-03-01 10:00 PDT - Temporary mitigation: pin customer to fp16 variant rw-13b-fp16-v1 for new sessions; immediate reduction in TTFB observed in canary traffic.
2026-03-02 11:30 PDT - Engineering reproduced in staging with synthetic workload; root cause investigation started.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Quantized variant kernel selection produced extra compile/compat checks on first request which serialized worker threads and delayed cache priming.
Hypothesis B: Autoscaling handoff logic invoked model cold-start path that did not reuse warmed KV cache; combined with continuous batching it caused request queueing and longer tail latency.
Evidence: Serving runtime logs show 'kernel_compile_check' events taking 800-1800ms on affected workers immediately prior to first token emission. These events correlated 1:1 with TTFB spikes.
Additional observation: The scheduler's 'handoff_grace' window was set to 2s; some handoffs extended beyond that and triggered fallback routing which added another 500-1200ms per request.
Related configs: Runtime feature flag 'auto-quant-handoff' was enabled in rollout group A on 2026-03-01.
comments: Asha Patel (Support) - 2026-03-01: Logged by customer. Requesting urgent SRE assistance; customer experiencing user-facing delays.
Miguel Ortega (SRE) - 2026-03-01: Triage complete. Pinning Ledgerly to fp16 variant as short-term mitigation while we investigate quant handoff path. Notified runtime/serving on-call.

Sara Kim (Serving Eng) - 2026-03-01: Observed kernel_compile_check spikes. Investigating why quant kernels require additional validation at handoff time. Moving to instrument tracing for compile path.
Ledgerly CS (Monica Reyes) - 2026-03-01: Appreciate the mitigation. Please keep us informed; several enterprise customers reported support tickets.

Miguel Ortega (SRE) - 2026-03-02: Reproduced in staging with synthetic long prompts + concurrent sessions. Confirmed increased KV-cache miss and compile check latency. Preparing PR to short-circuit compile check when compatible kernels cached.

Sara Kim (Serving Eng) - 2026-03-04: Deployed hotfix candidate to staging: skip redundant kernel-validate step when kernel binary digest matches known-compat map. Preliminary canary shows TTFB improvement from 2.4s -> 0.6s on first request.
resolution_notes: Short-term: Pinned Ledgerly to fp16 model variant for new sessions (completed 2026-03-01 10:00 PDT). Long-term: Applied hotfix to skip redundant kernel validation when digest matches known compatibility map (PR runtime/pull/1189). Deployed staged rollout 2026-03-04 and monitored canary for 24h; metrics show TTFB back to baseline and KV-cache warm-up behaviors normalizing. Follow-up: scheduler handoff grace logic will be adjusted (PR scheduler/pull/452) and additional canary gating added for future auto-quant rollouts.
